contentBlocks.text: This week you learned to analyze drama like a real literary critic. Let's review it all!

Quick review: drama is built from dialogue and stage directions, with no narrator (Day 1). Character is revealed through what someone says and does, sometimes contradicting each other (Day 2). Dramatic irony happens when the audience knows something a character doesn't (Day 3). You combined all three into one complete written analysis (Day 4). Explain in your own words why analyzing a play requires different skills than analyzing a novel.
Great work this week — you learned to analyze drama like a real literary critic! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review drama's structure, character-through-dialogue, and dramatic irony
Explain why analyzing drama requires different skills than analyzing prose
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child explain why drama analysis differs from novel analysis.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of drama-analysis skills!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the skill the child found most interesting this week (often dramatic irony) rather than requiring an even summary of all three
Ready for more: ask the child whether they think dramatic irony could also work in a novel, or whether it's unique to drama and film
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's three drama-analysis skills needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: Analyzing drama requires inferring meaning from dialogue, stage directions, and what a character does, since there's no narrator explaining thoughts or feelings directly — a reader has to actively interpret contradictions and gaps in knowledge (like dramatic irony) that a novel's narrator would usually spell out.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's Common Core Grade 9-10 literary-analysis-of-drama standards (RL.9-10.3/RL.9-10.4/RL.9-10.5) before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
